newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France little hit by Orly controllers.
newsitem.headline: Air France little hit by Orly controllers.

text.p: Air France said a 24-hour strike by air traffic controllers at Paris Orly airport, starting on the morning of April 30, would have little impact on its freighter flight programme.
"We expect to maintain all our long-haul programme of passenger and freighter flights from Paris-Orly to French overseas territories," an Air France official told Reuters.
Air France operates a 747-200F freighter flights on Wednesdays to the French West Indies (Pointe a Pitre and Fort de France) and to St Denis on the Indian Ocean island of Reunion, via Djibouti.

"As for our other freighter flights operating from Paris/Orly on Wednesdays, the timetabling of the New York-JFK service, scheduled to leave Wednesday evening, is subject to modification but the full details are not yet available," the official said.
There was no information at this stage on whether Air France's Wednesday freighter service between Paris/ Orly and Bogota in Colombia would operate as normal, the official added
The joint Air France/Tunis Air three-times weekly 737 freighter service would be affected by the controllers strike, a Tunis Air cargo official told Reuters.
"One of the 737 freighter flights operates on Wednesdays and this has been postponed until Thursday," the official said.
Globally, Air France expected to operate one out of two flights from Paris/Orly during the strike.

The 24-hour strike by Paris/Orly air traffic controllers, which is set to begin at 0600 local time (0400 GMT) on April 30, has been called to gain working conditions similar to their counterparts at Paris Charles de Gaulle airport.
A spokesman for France's aviation authority said overall, about 40 percent of scheduled traffic would be assured during the strike. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
